title: Production and Application of an Alishewanella jeotgali Strain HAQ8 Bioflocculant for Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbons (PAHs) Removal From Refinery Wastewater
content:
An extracellular bioflocculant produced by Alishewanella jeotgali HAQ8 achieved 82.12% PAHs removal from refinery wastewater under optimized conditions. Its carbohydrate-rich composition and effective treatment performance support its potential as a sustainable bio-based flocculant.


ABSTRACT

Polycyclic cyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) are widespread environmental pollutants associated with carcinogenic effects through various molecular mechanisms. High-molecular-weight PAHs (HMW-PAHs) are of particular concern because of their greater toxicity and environmental persistence. This study aimed to produce and characterize an extracellular bioflocculant from Alishewanella jeotgali strain HAQ8 isolated from oil refinery sludge in Basrah, Iraq, and evaluate its efficiency in removing polycyclic cyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) from refinery wastewater. An extracellular bioflocculant was extracted and characterized using UV–vis, TGA, FT-IR, SEM–EDX, LC–MS and zeta potential analysis. The bioflocculant was applied in Jar test to remove polycyclic cyclic aromatic hydrocarbons from refinery wastewater. The results showed that the bioflocculant was water-soluble and predominantly composed of carbohydrates (66%), including D-Allose (C6H12O6), sucrose (C12H22O11) and raffinose (C1₈H₃2O16). Eighteen PAHs compounds were identified in wastewater. The highest removal efficiency was 82.12% at pH 9, low mixing speed of 30 rpm, low mixing speed time of 6 min and settling time of 20 min. The bioflocculant showed potential as an environmentally sustainable alternative to synthetic flocculants for refinery wastewater.
